name: for Loop
description: Repeats a block of code a set number of times, controlled by an initializer, a condition, and an increment expression.
notes: Best suited when you need index access or a fixed iteration count.

name: for...in Loop
description: Iterates over the enumerable property names (keys) of an object, including inherited enumerable properties.
example: for (const key in { a: 1, b: 2 }) { console.log(key); } // 'a', 'b'
notes: Intended for object keys, not arrays — for arrays use for...of or forEach() to avoid iterating inherited/indexed quirks.

name: for...of Loop
description: Iterates over the values of any iterable object, such as arrays, strings, Maps, and Sets.
notes: Cannot be used directly on plain objects since they are not iterable — use Object.entries() with it instead.

name: while Loop
description: Repeats a block of code as long as a specified condition evaluates to true, checked before each iteration.
notes: If the condition never becomes false, the loop runs forever — ensure the loop body updates the condition.

name: do...while Loop
description: Repeats a block of code once before testing the condition, then continues while the condition remains true.
example: let i = 0; do { console.log(i); i++; } while (i < 3);
notes: Guarantees the loop body executes at least once, even if the condition is initially false.

name: break Statement
description: Immediately terminates the nearest enclosing loop or switch statement, resuming execution after it.
example: for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { if (i === 3) break; console.log(i); } // 0, 1, 2
notes: Can also be combined with a label to break out of an outer loop from within a nested one.

name: continue Statement
description: Skips the rest of the current loop iteration and proceeds to the next one.
example: for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if (i % 2 === 0) continue; console.log(i); } // 1, 3

name: Labeled Statements
description: A label identifies a loop so that break or continue can target it directly, even from inside a nested loop.
example: outer: for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { for (let j = 0; j < 3; j++) { if (j === 1) continue outer; console.log(i, j); } }
notes: Useful for breaking or continuing an outer loop from deeply nested loops, but overuse can hurt readability.
